segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: NASA's Artemis II will send four astronauts around the moon, preparing humanity for a

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: long-term lunar presence and future journeys to Mars.

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: Enabling communication and navigation for this test flight

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: are NASA's Near Space Network and Deep Space Network.

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: With antennas around the world and a fleet of relay satellites,

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: the networks will deliver vital data to and from Earth

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: through all phases of the mission.

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: The networks are seamlessly integrated

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: at NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston, Texas,

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: where mission control coordinates the network handovers.

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: These transfers represent a delicate dance between the two networks,

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: exchanging support as the mission shoots toward the moon.

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: On the launch pad and during their early orbit phases,

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: NASA's Orion spacecraft and Space Launch System rocket

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: will rely on communications and tracking services from the near-space network.

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: After its translunar injection burn,

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: the deep space network's global array of antennas

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: will serve as Orion's primary communications support during lunar orbit.

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: As the mission journeys farther into space and away from Earth,

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: Signal strength weakens, and bandwidth is conserved for crew communications.

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: The astronauts will have a near-constant connection to Earth,

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: ensuring their safety on a journey farther into space than ever before.

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: We say near-constance because as Orion goes behind the moon,

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: a planned loss in communications will occur.

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: The Deep Space Network will be standing by to reacquire the signal as Orion reappears.

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: The Artemis II mission also provides an opportunity to test new capabilities.

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: Using laser links, NASA will periodically transmit Orion data

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: to showcase the benefits laser communications could have for future human spaceflight missions.

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: The data from Orion, sent by radio signals or laser links, is massive.

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: The mission is gathering images, data, and video,

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: while also generating details about mission health and crew voice files.

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: All of that data gets processed here on Earth, where systems compress it for efficiency.

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: In the future, we'll upgrade these systems on Earth so that image and video clarity improve with each moon mission.

segments.speaker: PROMO_DSN
segments.text: With the Artemis II test flight, we're evaluating the communications infrastructure that will help carry us into the future as we explore the moon and journey forward to Mars.

segments.text: During the lunar flyby, and as part of Artemis II, it marked the first time in more than

segments.text: 50 years that humans were able to observe the moon directly and provided a critical

segments.speaker: ANNA_SCHNEIDER
segments.text: opportunity to practice how lunar science will be conducted during future Artemis missions.

segments.speaker: ANNA_SCHNEIDER
segments.text: The moon preserves a near-continuous record of solar system history that has been erased

segments.speaker: ANNA_SCHNEIDER
segments.text: on Earth, and with no atmosphere, weather,

segments.speaker: ANNA_SCHNEIDER
segments.text: or plate tectonics, the lunar surface retains evidence

segments.speaker: ANNA_SCHNEIDER
segments.text: of ancient impacts, volcanism, and solar activity

segments.speaker: ANNA_SCHNEIDER
segments.text: that scientists can study today.

segments.text: Studying the moon helps scientists understand how

segments.speaker: ANNA_SCHNEIDER
segments.text: planets formed and evolved,

segments.speaker: ANNA_SCHNEIDER
segments.text: how the moon influenced Earth's history,

segments.speaker: ANNA_SCHNEIDER
segments.text: and how the early sun shaped conditions

segments.speaker: ANNA_SCHNEIDER
segments.text: across the inner solar system.

segments.speaker: ANNA_SCHNEIDER
segments.text: The moon also serves as a unique platform

segments.speaker: ANNA_SCHNEIDER
segments.text: for studying the broader universe.
